fields.meta_title: Attendance Form Builder That Tracks Every Absence | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Create an attendance form that records absences and sign-ins by name, keeps a count per person, and alerts whoever acts. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Attendance Form That Counts Who Showed Up
fields.hero_description: Build an attendance form that matches each absence or sign-in to your roster and alerts you when a count passes your limit.
fields.features_heading: What Turns Sign-Ins Into an Attendance Record
fields.features_subheading: An attendance form template on a clipboard shows who came today. These pieces show who has been missing for weeks.
fields.feature_1:
Reports matched to your roster

Load the class list or staff list once. Each report or sign-in attaches to that person's record. A misspelled name never creates a second student or a duplicate employee.
fields.feature_2:
Reasons you can count later

Offer a short list of reasons, such as illness or an appointment, plus a note. Excused and unexcused absences are tallied apart, and each reason stays on the record by its date.
fields.feature_3:
Sign-in by QR code at the door

Print a code for the room or show it on a screen. People scan it with a phone camera and tap their name. Each sign-in is time-stamped, and anyone after the start time is marked late.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts at the number you choose

Pick the count that calls for action, like three call-outs in 30 days, and the person who acts on it. The app messages them in Slack or by email with a link to the record.
fields.feature_5:
A running total for everyone

Every report becomes a row in a database you own. Filter by name, week, or reason, compare attendance rates by class or shift, and export the rows when payroll asks for them.
fields.feature_6:
The app's source code, yours to keep

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can then host the attendance app on your servers or connect it to the school or HR system you run.

fields.usecase_heading: Where an Attendance Count Leads to Action
fields.tab_content_1:
After nine absences, Milo's name goes to the counselor

At 7:40 a.m., Priya Nair reports that Milo is home with a fever. Linden Elementary's office sees it on the grade 4 roster before the bell. Milo has now missed nine of 90 school days. The US Department of Education treats missing at least 10 percent of days as chronic absence, and the form adds him to the counselor's list.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every no-show is offered the next two sessions

Halden Freight's forklift refresher has 24 warehouse staff booked for 9:00 on Tuesday. A QR code on the training room door opens the sign-in, and each person taps their name. By 9:05, 21 have signed in. The three missing get an email with two new dates, and the trainer's roster shows who still owes the refresher.
fields.tab_content_3:
By Theo's third call-out in 30 days, Dana has a message

Theo Grant works the early pick shift at Corliss Supply. At 4:00 a.m., before his 6:00 a.m. start, he reports sick from the call-out form on his phone. It is his third call-out in 30 days. His supervisor, Dana Ruiz, gets a Slack message listing all three, and the shift lead sees 1 open spot on the pick line.
fields.tab_content_4:
Quorum met with 9 directors before the first vote

The Riverside Arts board has 15 directors, and its bylaws set quorum at 8. Before the quarterly meeting starts, each director signs in at the door or from a link inside the video call. The count reaches 9 at 6:04 p.m., the chair opens the first vote, and the secretary gets the list of who attended for the minutes.

fields.howto_title: How to Make an Attendance Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan the roster, fields, and alert rules for an attendance form that flags absences early, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the record is for
fields.howto_step_1_des: Settle the purpose before choosing fields. A school watches for chronic absence, a warehouse plans shifts around call-outs, and a board needs a quorum before it votes. That purpose sets which counts the form keeps and who hears about them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Start from the list of people you expect: students by class, staff by shift, directors by seat. A roster lets the form show who is missing, not only who turned up. Give each person one ID so records from different terms line up.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask only what the reporter knows at that moment, which is usually the name, the date, and a reason, with an optional note. A parent at 7:40 a.m. will not fill in eight fields. Offer reasons as a fixed list so they can be counted.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the number that should trigger action and who handles it, such as a ninth absence in 90 days or a third call-out in 30. Use the attendance policy your school or company already has instead of writing a new one.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Describe the form, the roster, the reasons, and the thresholds in plain English. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and the alert logic. Change any part later by prompting again, for example to add a QR sign-in for a second room.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send each alert to one named person, such as the counselor or the shift supervisor, and choose Slack or email for each. Give whoever reported an absence a confirmation screen and an email receipt. Nobody then has to call the office to check.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a test report for a made-up person who sits one absence below your threshold, then submit one more. Check that the count moves, the alert reaches the right person, and the record shows both dates. Delete the test rows before launch.

plan.angle: Seven of the top 10 are single schools' absence-reporting pages and the rest are printable record sheets (Personnel Concepts, Canva, a Tennessee school PDF). Each one collects a mark or a note and stops: someone still matches the report to a roster, counts absences by hand and notices a pattern weeks late. This page treats the attendance form as the record itself: every report or sign-in lands as a row against the roster, the counts keep themselves, and the person who acts hears when a threshold is crossed. It covers four settings searchers bring (a parent reporting a school absence, a QR sign-in at a training session, a shift worker calling out, a board meeting that needs a quorum) and stays off time-off requests, availability and class registration, which have their own pages.
tab_stories: A parent reports a fourth-grader sick before the bell, the office sees the report matched to the class roster, and because it is his ninth absence by day 90 the school counselor is flagged under the chronic absence rule of 10 percent.
Twenty-four warehouse staff are booked on a forklift refresher, 21 scan the QR code at the door by 9:05, and the three no-shows get an email with the next two dates to rebook.

A warehouse picker reports a call-out from his phone at 4:00 a.m., before his 6:00 a.m. start, the form logs it as his third in 30 days, and his supervisor gets a Slack message to schedule a conversation.

Directors of a nonprofit board sign in to the quarterly meeting in person or on the video call, the count reaches 9 of 15 against a bylaw quorum of 8, and the secretary gets the attendance list for the minutes.
